notes.claim: 1 cm is 10 mm, so a 1 cm square is 10 mm by 10 mm, which is 100 mm² and not 10.
1 m² equals 10,000 cm² (Bitesize works it from a 1 m by 1 m square drawn also as 100 cm by 100 cm).
The numbers to multiply or divide by are squared for area and cubed for volume.
Bitesize names the slip of thinking 100 cm² are needed for 1 m² because 1 m is 100 cm, and the same slip for volume.
Cable makers give conductor sizes in mm², and IEC 60228 sets the nominal cross-sectional areas.

The resistance, mass and cross-section of a round copper wire vary with the square of its diameter, so doubling the diameter quadruples the cross-section (the doubling step is arithmetic on the quote, not stated by the source).
